chunks: A number of our companions, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad al-Barqi, from Sharif ibn Sabiq, from al-Fadl ibn Abi Qurra, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

The Messenger of God (may God's blessings be upon him and his family) said: The disciples said to Isa, 'O Spirit of God! Whom should we sit with?' He said: 'One whose sight reminds you of God, and whose speech increases your knowledge, and whose deeds make you desirous of the Hereafter.'

key_terms.الحواريون: The disciples of Prophet Isa (Jesus); in Islamic tradition, the twelve devoted followers of Jesus
key_terms.روح الله: Spirit of God — a Quranic epithet for Prophet Isa (Jesus), emphasizing his miraculous, spirit-infused creation (Q 4:171)
key_terms.منطقه: His speech, discourse, articulation; in classical Arabic, manṭiq refers to well-ordered, eloquent expression
key_terms.نجالس: Sit with, keep company with; in Arabic scholarly tradition, majlis (gathering) is the primary vehicle of knowledge transmission
key_terms.يذكركم الله: Reminds you of God; spiritual remembrance (dhikr) evoked simply by presence, not words
key_terms.يرغبكم في الآخرة: Makes you desirous of the Hereafter; zuhd (asceticism) as demonstrated by the scholar's life, not just words

ai.seo_question: What are the qualities of a true scholar and companion according to Imam Sadiq and Jesus?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) relates a saying of the Prophet Muhammad (SAWW) in which the disciples of Prophet Isa (Jesus, peace be upon him) asked him about the qualities of the ideal companion and teacher. Isa's answer establishes three criteria: the scholar's very appearance should evoke consciousness of God, their words should impart knowledge, and their conduct should inspire longing for the Hereafter. This hadith was addressed to early Shia Muslims navigating a world of competing religious authorities, offering them a practical, observable criterion for identifying true scholars worthy of discipleship.
